items.title: ‘Bulldozer’: How Adeleke defeated APC, others to secure second term in Osun
items.description: By Nwafor Sunday, Online News Editor Governor Ademola Adeleke’s victory in the 2026 Osun State governorship election was driven by a combination of strong performances in his traditional strongholds, decisive victories in key local government areas and an ability to accumulate large vote margins that the All Progressives Congress (APC) could not overturn. The results from the 30 local government areas collated by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) showed Adeleke, who contested on the platform of the Accord Party, defeating the APC candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, in 19 local government areas, while the APC won 11. The African Democratic Congress (ADC), whose candidate was Najeem Salaam, finished a distant third in the three-party contest. The final figures for the three leading parties showed Accord polling 511,067 votes, against 444,815 votes for APC, while ADC recorded 17,180 votes. The figures gave Adeleke a 66,252-vote lead over his closest challenger. But beyond the numbers, Adeleke’s victory also reflected the confidence with which he entered the contest, having repeatedly dismissed concerns over the perceived political weight behind the APC campaign. Days before the election, the governor described himself as a “bulldozer”, declaring that he was not intimidated by what he characterised as federal might or the support of some governors for his opponent. ‘I am a bulldozer’ Speaking on Tuesday at the Arise Townhall Meeting, Adeleke said he was prepared to confront the political machinery backing the APC candidate. He said he was not afraid of the governors supporting Oyebamiji and challenged them to bring their full political weight into the contest. “I am a bulldozer. I am talk and do. I am not afraid of federal might and governors backing the APC candidate. If they like, they should bring all the governors,” Adeleke said. The declaration became a defining statement of the governor’s campaign as he sought to convince voters that the election would ultimately be decided by the people of Osun rather than the influence of political heavyweights outside the state. The results suggest that Adeleke was able to translate that confidence into a strong electoral performance. The mathematics of Adeleke’s victory The most revealing feature of the election was not simply the number of local governments won by each candidate, but the size of the margins recorded in their respective strongholds. Adeleke won 19 LGAs, while Oyebamiji carried 11. But some of Adeleke’s victories were particularly large, creating a substantial cushion that APC struggled to erase with its own victories. The clearest example came from the Ede axis. Ede delivered a huge advantage In Ede-North, Accord scored 35,427 votes, while APC recorded 10,283. That gave Adeleke a margin of 25,144 votes in one local government. The result in Ede-South was equally significant. Accord polled 26,188 votes, compared with APC’s 6,219, giving the governor another 19,969-vote advantage. Combined, the two Ede councils gave Accord 61,615 votes, against APC’s 16,502. That amounted to a 45,113-vote net advantage for Adeleke from just two LGAs. It was a margin that would prove difficult for APC to neutralise elsewhere. Osogbo adds to Adeleke’s advantage The state capital also contributed significantly to Adeleke’s performance. In Osogbo Local Government Area, Accord secured 36,480 votes, while APC polled 30,474. Adeleke therefore won the council by 6,006 votes. The ADC scored 1,503 votes in Osogbo, its strongest performance among the 30 LGAs covered by the supplied results. Osogbo was important not only because of its political significance but also because the result demonstrated Adeleke’s ability to remain competitive in an urban centre where APC also had considerable support. Adeleke dominates the Ife axis The Ife area was another important component of the governor’s victory. Accord won Ife-East, polling 27,201 votes against APC’s 18,600, a margin of 8,601 votes. In Ife-Central, Adeleke secured 21,171 votes, while APC recorded 15,913, giving Accord a further 5,258-vote advantage. Accord also won Ife-North, where it scored 13,879 votes against APC’s 9,613, a margin of 4,266 votes. APC, however, secured Ife-South, polling 14,678 votes against Accord’s 13,507, a margin of 1,171 votes. Overall, the four Ife councils produced 75,758 votes for Accord and 58,804 for APC, giving Adeleke a combined advantage of 16,954 votes. Egbedore, Iwo and Oriade strengthen the lead Adeleke’s victory was not confined to Ede, Osogbo and Ife. In Egbedore, Accord scored 19,278 votes, against APC’s 11,194, producing a margin of 8,084 votes. In Iwo, Adeleke polled 27,085 votes, while Oyebamiji recorded 19,660, giving Accord a margin of 7,425 votes. The governor also carried Oriade, where Accord secured 21,343 votes, compared with APC’s 14,863 — a difference of 6,480 votes. These victories helped Adeleke accumulate the substantial overall lead that emerged from the collation. APC remained a formidable challenger Despite losing the election, the results showed that APC remained a major political force in Osun. Oyebamiji won 11 of the 30 LGAs and recorded some impressive margins. His strongest performance in the supplied results came from Irewole, where APC polled 29,972 votes, against Accord’s 10,934. That gave APC a 19,038-vote advantage in the local government. APC also won Boripe, with 19,963 votes against Accord’s 12,448, a margin of 7,515 votes. It further secured victories in Olorunda, Ilesa-East, Ife-South, Ola-Oluwa, Isokan, Obokun, Atakumosa-West and Atakumosa-East. But the challenge for APC was the distribution and size of those victories. The party won several LGAs, but its combined margins were not enough to offset the much larger margins accumulated by Adeleke in his strongest areas. Adeleke won big where it mattered The 2026 election therefore provides an interesting lesson in electoral mathematics. A candidate does not necessarily need to win every local government to secure a statewide victory. What matters is the aggregate vote total. Adeleke’s 19 victories produced 511,067 votes, while APC’s 11 winning LGAs contributed to an overall total of 444,815 votes. The difference was 66,252 votes. The Ede results alone accounted for a substantial portion of that overall margin. This explains why APC’s victories in several councils, including Irewole and Boripe, were insufficient to overturn Adeleke’s advantage. The ADC factor The ADC did not come close to challenging either Accord or APC for overall victory, but its performance remains relevant to the analysis. The party polled 17,180 votes across the 30 LGAs. Its strongest showing among the supplied results came in Ejigbo, where it scored 5,053 votes. It also recorded 1,503 in Osogbo, 935 in Ife-East, 747 in Ife-Central, and 673 each in Ifedayo and Ilesa-West. In most other LGAs, however, its votes were significantly lower. The ADC therefore emerged as a third force in pockets of the state but did not acquire enough support to seriously threaten the two leading candidates. A two-party contest despite 13 candidates Thirteen candidates contested the governorship election, but the results demonstrated the dominance of the two leading parties. Yet, the election quickly became a contest dominated by Accord and APC. The combined Accord and APC figures stood at 955,882 votes, compared with 17,180 votes recorded by ADC. That concentration of votes underscored the strength of the two principal political camps. Adeleke’s geographical spread Another important factor in the election was the geographical spread of Adeleke’s victories. His 19 LGAs were spread across different parts of the state. He won Ede-North, Ede-South, Osogbo, Ife-Central, Ife-East, Ila, Boluwaduro, Irepodun, Ayedire, Ejigbo, Ayedaade, Ifelodun, Ife-North, Ilesa-West, Egbedore, Orolu, Oriade, Ifedayo, Odo-Otin and Iwo, based on the results supplied. This spread gave his campaign a broad electoral base. Rather than depending exclusively on one bloc, Adeleke combined overwhelming support in some councils with competitive performances across others. APC’s strongholds could not compensate Oyebamiji’s 11 victories showed that APC had considerable support across Osun. But the party’s biggest problem was that some of its strongest victories came in areas where Accord’s losses were relatively manageable, while Adeleke was simultaneously building enormous advantages elsewhere. For example, APC’s 19,038-vote advantage in Irewole was significant. But Adeleke’s 45,113-vote combined advantage in Ede-North and Ede-South alone was more than twice the Irewole margin. That is the central arithmetic behind the election. APC won some areas decisively. Adeleke won some areas even more decisively. And the latter proved more consequential when all the votes were aggregated. The significance of Ede The Ede results deserve particular attention because they illustrate the scale of the governor’s political strength. Adeleke did not merely win Ede-North and Ede-South. He dominated them. In Ede-North, Accord secured more than three times APC’s vote. In Ede-South, it secured more than four times the APC vote. Together, the two councils generated a margin of 45,113 votes. In a contest ultimately decided by a statewide difference of 66,252 votes, the importance of those two local governments cannot be overstated. From “bulldozer” claim to ballot-box numbers Before the election, Adeleke’s “bulldozer” declaration was essentially a political challenge: a statement that the presence of federal power and governors backing his opponent would not determine the outcome in Osun. The results provide the numerical context for that claim. His campaign succeeded in producing overwhelming margins in areas such as Ede-North and Ede-South, while maintaining enough support in other parts of the state to win 19 LGAs. The APC, despite its institutional and political strength, could not translate its 11 local government victories into enough votes to close the statewide gap. In that sense, the election became a test not merely of political influence but of how effectively each side converted its support into actual votes. And on the figures available, Adeleke’s side did that more effectively. The final picture The 2026 Osun governorship election was ultimately a contest between two dominant political structures. APC demonstrated that it remained a formidable force, winning 11 LGAs and posting large margins in some of them. But Adeleke’s Accord Party carried 19 LGAs and, more importantly, produced sufficiently large margins in key councils to establish a lead that APC could not overcome. The final figures tell the story: Accord — 511,067 votes APC — 444,815 votes ADC — 17,180 votes Accord’s lead over APC — 66,252 votes Adeleke’s victory was therefore not simply about winning 19 local governments against APC’s 11. It was about where he won, how many votes he accumulated there and the size of the margins he created. Ede-North and Ede-South provided the biggest cushion. Osogbo strengthened the position. The Ife axis broadened the advantage, while victories in Egbedore, Iwo, Oriade and other councils prevented APC from closing the gap. Before the election, Adeleke had presented himself as a “bulldozer”, insisting that he was not intimidated by federal might or the governors backing his opponent. After the votes were counted, the numbers showed that the governor had indeed built a formidable electoral advantage. Adeleke won 19 LGAs, polled 511,067 votes and defeated APC by 66,252 votes — putting him on course for a second term in Osun State. The post ‘Bulldozer’: How Adeleke defeated APC, others to secure second term in Osun appeared first on Vanguard News .

Adeleke secured 511,067 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Bola Oyebamiji of the All Progressives Congress (APC), who polled 444,815 votes. items.title: Le poème du dimanche | ‘‘Le cadeau du printemps’’ de Fadhila Messai
items.description: Née en 1966 à Gafsa, Fadhila Messai ( فضيلة مسعي ) , est écrivain et journaliste. Romancière, poète et critique. Après des études supérieures en sociologie, elle poursuit des recherches universitaires en littérature. A l’origine de la fondation de Radio Gafsa, elle y est reconnue et réputée comme journaliste culturelle Son œuvre littéraire compte de nombreux ouvrages : romans, recueils de poésie et essais, traduits et couronnés de diverses distinctions internationales. Parmi ses recueils de poésie, (en arabe) : «Une femme de feu » ; «L’hémorragie de la neige» ; « Le nectar de la passion» ; « Le camp de l’amour» . Tahar Bekri Quand j’étais jeune fille A haute voix je psalmodiais au printemps ses nombreuses histoires Je portais ses lettres amoureuses à une rose Une fleur Une tulipe endormie dans un bosquet Et tout innocence je courais sur les montagnes hautes Je m’arrêtais sur les collines Sur les cimes Je ramassais les étoiles dans mon panier Leur donnais la truffe enfouie dans mes yeux Leur recommandais le bon voisinage de la lune Je refusais les bijoux du monde Ses diamants Et quelques autres pierres précieuses Me suffisais du présent modeste du printemps Un bel œillet qui orne mes cheveux Pour écrire sur son amour sa fascination mon meilleur poème Traduit de l’arabe par Tahar Bekri Extrait de »Dans le creux de tes yeux », inédit (Remerciements à l’auteure). items.title: Un bus se renverse à Naâma : six morts et 31 blessés
items.description: Nouvel accident tragique de bus en Algérie. Cette fois, le drame s’est produit à Naâma. Un autobus de la marque Higer a dérapé avant de se renverser sur la RN 6 à Aïn Sefra ce dimanche 16 août à l’aube. Le bilan est lourd : six morts et 31 blessés, a indiqué la Protection civile. « Nos équipes sont intervenues à 03 h 05 après le dérapage et le renversement d’un autobus sur la RN6 à Aïn Sefra », a indiqué la même source. Un camion d’intervention et deux ambulances ont été mobilisés par la Protection civile dans cette opération. Les photos de l’accident montrent un bus couché sur le côté avec d’importants dégâts matériels. Les circonstances et les causes de ce nouveau drame routier n’ont pas été précisées. Accidents de bus en Algérie : la série noire se poursuit Le 31 juillet, un accident de bus à Boumerdès a fait 28 morts et 39 blessés. Le lendemain, quatre personnes ont perdu la vie et 43 autres ont été blessées dans un nouveau drame routier impliquant un autobus de transport de voyageurs à Timimoun. Cinq jours plus tard, un autre accident de bus a fait six morts et 19 blessés à Constantine. Après cette série tragique, les services de sécurité ont lancé une vaste opération de contrôle des bus à travers le territoire national, avec des tests de drogue systématiques sur les chauffeurs. L’article Un bus se renverse à Naâma : six morts et 31 blessés est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Biat Privilèges | Une marketplace bancaire dédiée aux avantages clients
items.description: La Biat annonce le lancement de Biat Privilèges, une nouvelle application permettant l’accès à une marketplace bancaire qui offre un large univers de réductions et d’offres exclusives négociées auprès de centaines d’enseignes partenaires. A travers cette nouvelle offre innovante, la Biat enrichit l'expérience de ses clients au-delà des services bancaires traditionnels et contribue à renforcer leur relation avec la banque. Dans le cadre de sa stratégie d’innovation et d’amélioration continue de l’expérience client, la Biat poursuit le développement de solutions à valeur ajoutée pour répondre aux nouvelles attentes et aux habitudes de sa clientèle. C’est dans cette dynamique que la banque lance Biat Privilèges, une nouvelle application extra-bancaire permettant à ses clients de bénéficier d’avantages exclusifs auprès d'une large sélection de marques et d’enseignes partenaires. Cette initiative traduit la volonté de la Biat d'enrichir sa proposition de valeur à travers une offre qui permet à ses clients de réaliser des économies sur leurs dépenses courantes, leurs loisirs et leurs projets de consommation. Elaborée en partenariat avec FreeOui et d’autres partenaires de référence, l’application donne accès à plus de 450 enseignes représentant plus de 1 300 points de vente répartis sur l'ensemble du territoire tunisien. Les clients de la Biat peuvent ainsi bénéficier d’avantages exclusifs dans de nombreux univers de consommation tels que le shopping, les loisirs, les voyages, la restauration, le bien-être, la santé et la culture. Pensée pour être simple, rapide et accessible, Biat Privilèges permet aux utilisateurs de consulter les offres organisées par thématique et profiter des avantages proposés, en fonction de leurs centres d’intérêt et de leur localisation. items.title: Camp vacances Faso Mêbo à Dédougou : le Camarade ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, Mikaïlou Sidibé, échange avec les campeurs
items.description: ‎Le Camarade ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, Mikaïlou Sidibé, accompagné des autorités administratives et militaires, a rendu visite le 15 août 2026 aux jeunes du Camp vacances Faso Mêbo réunis à Dédougou. Cette immersion auprès des campeurs de la 5ème région militaire visait à saluer l'engagement des enfants et de leurs encadreurs dans cette deuxième édition, pensée comme un véritable cadre d'apprentissage, de divertissement et d'éveil citoyen. ‎‎Lors de ses échanges avec la jeunesse, le Camarade ministre a insisté sur l'importance de cultiver des valeurs cardinales telles que la solidarité, la discipline et le patriotisme, tout en bannissant la paresse, le vol et le mensonge. Il a vivement invité les Campeurs à s'inspirer des grandes figures de l'histoire du Burkina Faso, à honorer le sacrifice des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), et à grandir avec un « esprit militaire » guidé par le sens du devoir. ‎Au-delà de l'éducation morale, le camarade Mikaïlou Sidibé a encouragé les campeurs à s'approprier les ateliers pratiques, notamment l’initiation à la confection de pavés, indispensables pour faire d'eux les futurs bâtisseurs de la Nation. Joignant l'acte à la parole, l'autorité ministérielle a d'ailleurs mis la main à la pâte en fabriquant des pavés aux côtés des jeunes, illustrant par l'exemple l'importance de l'effort collectif. ‎Cette visite de terrain s'est achevée dans une ambiance fraternelle autour du partage de la soupe de midi avec les Campeurs . À travers ces moments de proximité et la vision globale du camp Faso Mêbo, les autorités réaffirment leur ambition majeure , forger une jeunesse disciplinée, solidaire et profondément engagée pour la souveraineté et le développement du Burkina Faso. ‎Direction des Affaires juridiques et de la communication de l’Agence Faso Mêbo

items.title: Osun Election: Adeleke wins 19 LGAs, Oyebamiji takes 11
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Following the conclusion of collation of results at the headquarters of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Osun State, Governor Ademola Adeleke has won 19 of the 30 local government areas in the state. The results were collated in the early hours of Sunday by the respective Local Government Area (LGA) collation officers following the conclusion of voting on Saturday. Adeleke won in Ede-North, Ede-South, Osogbo, Ife-Central, Ife-East, Ila, Boluwaduro, Irepodun, Ayedire, Ejigbo and Ayedaade LGAs. He also won in Ifelodun, Ife-North, Ilesa-West, Egbedore, Orolu, Oriade, Ifedayo, Odo-Otin and Iwo LGAs. Meanwhile, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, won in Olorunda, Irewole, Ilesa-East, Ife-South, Ola-Oluwa, Isokan, Boripe, Obokun, Atakumosa-West and Atakumosa-East LGAs. However, Irepodun was listed among both Adeleke’s and Oyebamiji’s winning LGAs in the supplied copy and should be verified against the official collation sheet. The Chief Returning Officer for the election, Professor Joshua Ogunwole, Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University Oye-Ekiti, is yet to formally declare the winner. The declaration will follow the completion of the final collation and verification of the results by INEC. items.title: Bribe fails as Bauchi police arrest two over cattle rustling
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two suspects in Alkaleri Local Government Area over alleged possession of rustled cattle and an attempt to bribe police officers with N400,000 to compromise the investigation. The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement, saying operatives recovered three of the rustled cattle and intercepted the alleged bribe money. According to him, the incident followed a report lodged on August 6, 2026, by two residents of Yalo Village, who alleged that unknown gunmen had rustled 103 cattle belonging to them from the Yankari Forest in July. Habib said police operatives subsequently traced the movement of the cattle to Mararaban Liman Katagum, where the victims identified three of the missing animals. He said, following a tip-off and assistance from a traditional ruler, the police arrested two suspects on August 7. The suspects were identified as Abdullahi Adamu, 26, of Jarmai Village, Dangi Local Government Area of Plateau State, and Muktashir Idris, 20, also of Jarmai Village. During interrogation, Idris allegedly told the police that his master, identified as Alaba, had sent him to the market to sell the stolen cattle. The PPRO said the investigation took another turn when a brother of one of the victims informed detectives that Alaba had allegedly sent N400,000 to compromise the case and stop the police investigation. According to him, the brother had earlier offered to assist security agents in luring and arresting the prime suspect but was unsuccessful. Police operatives, however, intercepted and recovered the N400,000, which has been registered as an exhibit. The Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, has ordered the immediate transfer of the case to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) for further investigation. The command said its operatives were intensifying efforts to arrest Alaba, while the two suspects in custody would be charged to court upon completion of the investigation. Aliyu urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious movements of livestock and other criminal activities to the nearest police station. items.title: OLUBUNMI TUNJI-OJO: Beyond passport reforms
items.description: By Olufemi Salako When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu promised Nigerians a Renewed Hope Agenda, the skepticism among Nigerians was so strong because of many unfulfilled campaign promises, and were dismissive of it as another hope raised to soon be dashed. While some school of thoughts were of the opinion that the new administration should be given a benefit of the doubt, both skeptics and optimists agreed it will take a while for the vision and promises to become a reality and definitely not in four years, or first term of the Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s presidency. At the mention of Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, the Honourable Minister of Interior, what comes to mind of many Nigerians is the repositioned, reformed, and reorganized Nigeria Immigration Service and passport services. Nigerians now get value for money as obtaining a new passport or renewing it is now seamless, hitch free, without being fleeced by immigration officials or extorted because of a passport racketeering. I’m here to tell you there is more to him beyond easement of various passport services by NIS, there are bold reforms across all the services under his administrative control. The reforms are so defining and far reaching that the impact is evident in just three years in office as Minister and also as one of the brightest light of the Renewed Hope Agenda of the present administration. Digital transformation He started out with the drive of digital transformation of public service delivery by replacing manual processes with technology-driven systems, which is a clear demonstration of him bringing his professional background and training to bear. Most of the reforms embarked upon by him are hinged on technological innovation or introduction. It is in furtherance of this that he mandated the strict institutional digitization and enterprise content management systems (Interas) across the ministry to enforce transparency and curb bureaucratic inefficiency. This further promoted institutional discipline as the hallmark of that policy is electronic correspondence across departments and agencies of the ministry of Interior. There is no way we will talk about the many reforms embarked upon by Tunji-Ojo, especially the technologically driven reforms without a quick mention of how such digitization move resolved the NIN (National Identification Number) modification backlog. This move tackled and resolved an inherited backlog of roughly 2.5million requests. This was critical to the efficiency in the process of renewing or obtaining new passport which is widely celebrated. It must also be stated that the ongoing reforms, e-gates were deployed at major international airports to streamline processing and elevate border surveillance. He didn’t stop at reforms aimed at improving service delivery of agencies under his oversight control, he went beyond improving institutional framework and improved on the welfare, and working conditions across these agencies in what turned out to be a major boost to their motivation, the productivity and efficiency as well. To achieve this, he first embarked on prisons decongestion by raising significant funds via public-private partnerships to pay off fines for minor offenders, thereby freeing over 4,000 inmates and cutting feeding expenditures. This also reduced the burden of managing inmates in overcrowded prison facilities. He then recruited scores of medical personnel and upgraded infrastructure and health standards across custodial centers and this was responsible for the first-ever major surgery performed on an inmate at the Kuje Correctional Facility. This has made our correctional facilities live up to its core mandates of being a rehabilitation and reformative centers, and not where people come out worse off than they went in. Oversight powers It is on record that he had personally intervened and brought his oversight powers to bear when there is need for such and two instances come to mind when he ordered probe into act of misconduct by personnel of the Nigeria Correctional Service (NCoS). The first had to do with allegations of corruption and reprehensible behaviour, when it was alleged that Idris Okuneye (known as Bobrisky) who was an inmate in one of the correctional facility slept outside the prison walls during his six-month sentence. In a clear departure from past experiences where nothing comes out of such probe, or often times, that no culpability is established, the probe confirmed irregularities, including unauthorized special privileges and a furnished single cell. Further findings of the Probe as established by the panel stated that Bobrisky remained inside the custodial center. The panel also noted procedural violations and backdated documentation regarding his transfers between custodial centers and also affirmed that evidence showed he had unauthorized access to communication devices and frequent, unrestricted visits. This prompted disciplinary actions to be taken on some Senior NCoS officers while Michael Anugwa and Sikiru Adekunle, and other top controllers at Kirikiri were suspended to allow for an unbiased investigation. This was a demonstration of zero tolerance for indiscipline, unprofessionalism and corruption which had plagued the service before Tunji-Ojo resumed office as Minister of Interior. It also demonstrated his unflinching dedication that there shall be no compromise on the core values of integrity, transparency, and accountability of any agency under the administrative control of the Ministry under his watch. Same standard and procedure were extended to the allegations of misconduct and criminal activities within the Okere Correctional Centre in Warri, Delta State. Aftermath of the investigations led authorities to move more than 150 prisoners from Okere to custodial facilities in northern Nigeria while the Minister instituted wide-ranging administrative reviews and personnel removals to crack down on compromised internal security protocols. It is noteworthy that since he assumed office, there had been no jailbreak, something which was a regular occurrence in the last five years. Also in his three years in office, there had been a massive career progression which ended prolonged career stagnation by ensuring timely yearly promotion exercises for thousands of paramilitary personnel across immigration, correctional, and civil defense units. This resulted in over 100,000 paramilitary officers promoted within two years, while recruitment approvals were secured for 30,000 personnel, and a Paramilitary Pensions Board established to address long-standing retirement anxieties. He made the signing of Performance Bond with Head of agencies under him more than a ritual, but a call to service to see them actively deliver on their yearly operational targets. Recently, during the signing of 2026 performance bond with the service heads, he made them to see it as proof of commitment to fulfillment of mandates after a performance review by the agencies. The minister commended the services for their dedication, focus and tremendous contribution to nation building, noting that to whom much was given much was expected, as President Bola Tinubu had invested his trust in them, so there was no room to betray the trust. Lastly, the peak of the many reforms embarked by him, and exemplary leadership is evident in enhanced and improved operational capabilities of all the agencies under his supervision. Two instances of such are the establishment of specialized units as dedicated response groups, such as the Mining Marshals and specialized railway commands under the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), to safeguard critical national infrastructure. Also the massive investments in Federal Fire Service by expanding its logistics and fleet deployments for the Federal Fire Service, reducing overall national property loss from fire incidents. One thing is evident, Tunji-Ojo is not just one of the many flash in the pan, or what we call “initial gra gra” in our local parlance exhibited by political appointees we have lived with, he is real, he is true and he is our reality which tells us that we will get it right as a nation. The post OLUBUNMI TUNJI-OJO: Beyond passport reforms appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ABACHA: 28 years on, still no evidence
items.description: By Dan Etete I have read the claims made by Mr Dennis Amachree in his memoir concerning the death of General Sani Abacha, as reported by a newspaper on July 21, 2026. Mr Amachree asks Nigerians to accept a detailed account of the final hours of a Head of State on nothing but his own recollection, offered twenty-eight years after the fact. He names no witness. The woman on whom his entire account depends is not identified. There is nothing to show she has ever confirmed a word of it. He produces no post-mortem. No record of the interrogation he says he conducted. No file number, no signed statement, no duty log, no visitor’s book, no medical finding from anyone qualified to make one. He places a quotation in the mouth of a person he will not name and asks us to treat it as history. He tells us the time to the minute. He tells us the room. He tells us what was said. Twenty-eight years on, from memory, with nothing on paper behind any of it. He is careful to dismiss every other account for lacking evidence. He then offers his own on precisely the same footing. So let the questions be asked plainly. Where is the post-mortem report? Who is this woman, is she alive, and has she confirmed this? Where is the record of the interrogation — the date, the place, the signature? What file number covers it? Who was the officer he says he telephoned, and has that man corroborated a word? What flight manifest, what hotel register, what duty log supports any part of this timeline? On what medical authority was a cause of death determined, and by whom? None of these are unreasonable questions. Every one of them should have an answer. Not one of them has been answered. I do not write as a lawyer or a spokesman for General Abacha. I served in that government. I knew the man, and I know him as a close friend. And I am telling you plainly: I do not believe a word of this. In twenty-eight years, through every inquiry and every commission, through all the years when the people close to that night were still alive and still talking, this account was never once raised. Not to me. Not to anyone I know. It surfaces now, for the first time, in a book with a price on it I do not pretend the record of those years is beyond argument. It is not, and it will be argued over long after all of us are gone. But a man’s death is not entertainment, and a country’s history is not built on the unsupported memory of one man. I cannot tell you what is in Mr Amachree’s mind. I can tell you what is in his hands: nothing. No post-mortem. No file. No signature. No woman. He did not provide any evidence because they do not exist. Now, for clarity, please address the following as well: What are the so-called woman’s name and her nationality? Why did you allow her to leave the country without filing a serious criminal investigation against her? Who ordered her release and subsequent departure from Nigeria? Gen. Sani Abacha was not an ordinary man or citizen of Nigeria. For such an important case which involves the country’s president, it should not be taken lightly and handled by you alone. Let me be very clear here that you are simply seeking cheap publicity and relevance. Until the author provides verified, documented answers to those questions — names, nationality, investigation records, authorization for release, and supporting documentary evidence — no serious reader should treat this account as anything more than an unsubstantiated narrative. The account remains unverified, unsupported, and unconvincing. It should not be trusted. It reads as little more than a salacious attempt to attract attention and sell a book. •Etete is a former Minister of Petroluem Resources The post ABACHA: 28 years on, still no evidence appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: BLACK JULY:Benue killings worsen after Miyetti Allah leader shot dead
items.description: Attacks turn communities into fields of fear By Peter Duru, Makurdi For generations, the people of Benue South have been known for their resilience, rich cultural heritage and agricultural prowess. Stretching across communities where farming is more than an occupation but a way of life, the district has long been regarded as one of the food-producing hubs of Nigeria. Today, however, the songs of harvest have largely been replaced by the echoes of gunfire, cries of bereaved families and the silence of deserted villages. In what residents describe as one of the darkest periods in the history of the zone, communities across Otukpo, Ohimini, Okpokwu LGAs, and neighbouring areas have come under relentless attacks by suspected armed herders. Hardly a week passed without reports of fresh killings, kidnappings, cattle rustling or the displacement of entire communities. Although attacks have plagued parts of Benue State for years, many residents believe the crisis assumed a more frightening dimension following the June 26, 2026, assassination of the Benue State Chairman of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Ardo Risku Muhammad, and his associate, Yakubu Isah. The two men were reportedly ambushed and killed at Okudu village in Otukpo LGA while returning from a peace mission at Idekpa in neighbouring Ohimini LG. The murder of Ardo Risku which was widely condemned by leaders from within and outside the state appeared to usher in another cycle of bloodshed across the district. Since that incident, Benue South has witnessed a disturbing succession of attacks, with victims ranging from farmers and traders to clerics, academics, women, children and travellers. Communities that once bustled with commercial and farming activities now live under constant fear of the next attack. In many of the affected villages, residents now sleep with one eye open. Some have abandoned their ancestral homes altogether, while others have restricted farming activities for fear of being ambushed on their way to the fields. For a region where agriculture sustains families and local economies, the consequences have been devastating. Mood A community leader in Otukpo, reflecting the mood across the district, lamented: “People no longer think about harvest. Every day is about survival. We don’t know who will be attacked next or which village will be invaded.” The fear gripping Benue South has been reinforced by the frequency of attacks recorded within a few weeks. Hardly had one community begun mourning its dead before another was thrown into grief, creating an atmosphere of uncertainty that continues to spread across the district. Among the incidents that deepened public anxiety was the reported killing of former Benue State Secretary to the State Government, Prof. David Salifu, who was allegedly ambushed by suspected armed men along the Wukari–Joota Road in Katsina-Ala LGA, a border community between Benue and Taraba states. The wave of insecurity spared neither religious institutions nor their leaders. The abduction of Senior Pastor of the Universal Reformed Christian Church (NKST), Rev. Dr. Samuel Gbinde, alongside two members of his congregation at Andyar community in Guma LGA sent another chilling message that even places of worship had become vulnerable. Residents said the incidents reinforced fears that no one was safe anymore. As the Secretary of the Campaign for Equal Rights and Opportunities for all Nigerians (CERON) Francis Odiir puts it, “When professors, pastors, farmers and ordinary villagers are all targets, it means nobody can truly say they are safe.” The attacks intensified as July unfolded, with virtually every week bringing fresh reports of bloodshed. Communities across Benue South and other parts of the state became theatres of violence, leaving behind a trail of deaths, injuries, displacement and shattered livelihoods. On July 1, suspected armed herdsmen reportedly attacked Sai community in Mbajir Council Ward of Katsina-Ala Local Government Area, killing no fewer than 10 persons and injuring more than 15 others. The attack, carried out in the early hours of the day, further heightened fears that rural communities had become easy targets for armed groups. Barely 24 hours later, another tragedy struck in Okpokwu LGA. Armed cattle rustlers, believed to be herders, reportedly attacked Okpafie community in Oyilawu, killing a ranch owner and a member of the local vigilante before making away with nearly 50 cattle. On July 4, suspected armed herders launched a two-day assault on communities in Kwande LGA. Four persons were reportedly killed while at least 10 others sustained injuries. Farmers working on their farmlands and travellers attempting to flee the attack were said to be among the victims. The attacks reached another tragic milestone on July 9 when renowned historian and former Head of the Department of History at Benue State University, Professor Gabriel Nyityo, was reportedly murdered by a suspected armed herder at his residence on the outskirts of Makurdi. His killing sent shockwaves across the academic community and underscored the widening reach of insecurity in the state. Three days later, Benue South suffered one of its deadliest attacks in recent months. Suspected armed herdsmen invaded Akpachi village in Ugboju community, killing two farmers on their farmland. Before grieving families could recover from that tragedy, the attackers struck again less than 24 hours later. At about 4am the following day, the gunmen reportedly invaded Otukpo-Nobi community, killing at least 16 persons and injuring several others. The coordinated attacks deepened fears that communities were facing an organised campaign of violence with devastating consequences for residents. Survivor’s harrowing experience One resident who survived the Otukpo-Nobi attack recalled the terrifying experience, saying, “We woke up to the sound of gunfire. People ran in different directions, but many never made it. By sunrise, our community had become a place of mourning.” The cycle of violence continued on July 14 when suspected armed herdsmen reportedly attacked Ondo community in Ugboju District of Otukpo LGA. One person was killed, several houses were abandoned and frightened residents fled into nearby communities in search of safety. Two days later, Ankpechi community along the Otukpo-Ogobia Road in Ohimini LGA came under attack. Armed men reportedly shot a resident and looted several provision stores, leaving business owners counting heavy losses while residents questioned the absence of effective security protection. As the attacks spread from one community to another, many displaced families found refuge in neighbouring towns, schools, churches and makeshift camps. Their stories were remarkably similar, homes abandoned overnight, farms left untended, businesses destroyed and an uncertain future hanging over thousands of innocent people. The insecurity took yet another disturbing turn on July 19 when three siblings travelling from Abuja to Benue with the remains of their late mother were reportedly abducted along the Ogobia-Otukpo Road in Ohimini LGA. The victims were said to have been conveying their mother’s body to their hometown in Okpokwu LGA for burial when they were intercepted by suspected armed herdsmen between Omutele and Ankpechi communities and held them hostage. The incident left many residents heartbroken. A journey meant to give a deceased mother a dignified burial ended in tragedy, highlighting the growing dangers confronting travellers on major roads across Benue South. For many families, even mourning has become fraught with fear. Fresh violence erupted on July 21 when suspected armed herdsmen reportedly attacked Sai community in Katsina-Ala LGA killing at least 10 persons and injuring more than 15 others. The attack prompted Governor Hyacinth Alia to order security agencies to track down the perpetrators and restore calm to the affected communities. Just a day later, gunmen reportedly invaded Olahimu village in Ogoli Ugboju, Otukpo LGA, killing a 15-year-old boy and rustling several cattle. The death of the teenager underscored the painful reality that children have not been spared in the escalating violence. On July 27, fresh attacks on communities in Ohimini and Ukum LGAs claimed at least four lives, including a mother, while several residents, among them children, suffered severe machete injuries. Local vigilantes and community volunteers continued searching nearby bushes for missing persons long after the attackers had fled. The bloodshed persisted into July 28 when separate attacks in Otukpo and Kwande LGA reportedly claimed no fewer than 16 lives. Several other victims sustained serious injuries, while motorcycles belonging to fleeing farmers were reportedly carted away by the attackers. For many residents, the repeated attacks have gone beyond statistics. Behind every casualty figure is a grieving family, an orphaned child, a widowed spouse, an abandoned farm and a community struggling to rebuild amid recurring violence. Entire villages that once thrived on farming and commerce now live under the shadow of fear and uncertainty. A resident of one of the affected communities, James Abah, captured the mood of many survivors, saying, “we no longer know what tomorrow holds. We only pray every night that our village will not be the next to be attacked.” Community leaders, traditional rulers and religious organisations have repeatedly appealed to the Federal government and security agencies to strengthen security operations across Benue South. They insist that only sustained military presence, improved intelligence gathering, effective policing and the prosecution of those responsible for the attacks can restore confidence among residents. Security experts also argue that beyond military action, lasting peace will require dialogue, justice for victims, accountability for perpetrators and practical measures to address the root causes of recurring violence. Without these, they warn, the cycle of attacks may continue to deepen humanitarian and economic challenges in the region. As Benue South mourns its dead and counts the cost of months of relentless violence, one message echoes across its battered communities: peace has become the people’s greatest aspiration. Until the killings end and displaced families can safely return to their homes and farms, the district that once symbolised abundance will remain a painful reminder of the human cost of insecurity in Nigeria. items.title: Rampant Bangladesh make history with first-ever Test win in Australia
items.description: A dominant Bangladesh stunned hosts Australia to win the first Test by nine wickets in Darwin on Sunday for a historic maiden Test victory on Australian soil. After bowling Australia out for 284 and needing 57 to win, the visitors cruised past the total when Mominul Haque slashed Beau Webster to the backward point boundary. Bangladesh dominated Australia throughout the match and the margin of victory will send shockwaves through the cricketing world. After bowling Australia out for 198 in the first innings, the visitors always looked the more likely to win. They kept the pressure on throughout Sunday and didn’t panic when Cameron Green (104) brought up his third Test century after lunch on day four. Green was offered no real support from his teammates and the Bangladeshis kept taking vital scalps to leave Australia on the ropes, with Mehidy Hasan Miraz taking 5-66. The visitors went into the match with most observers giving them no chance of winning. Their only warm-up game, against a Cricket Australia XI, ended in a big loss that included a second-innings collapse where they were all out for 54. But they have completely outplayed the Australians and won every session, batting, bowling and catching better than their more illustrious counterparts. Australia, fielding their best possible team, have looked out of sorts from the beginning. Their batting failed in the first innings when they were bowled out on the opening day, then their much-vaunted bowling attack struggled against the gritty Bangladesh batsmen. Led by a maiden Test century from opener Tanzid Hasan , Bangladesh made 426 and importantly kept Australia in the field for 138 overs in Darwin’s heat and humidity. The bowlers then showed great patience Saturday to make regular breakthroughs and keep Australia under the cosh. When Australia resumed Sunday on 161-4, most of their hopes lay with Alex Carey and Green. Carey lived dangerously in the opening 30 minutes, twice edging seamer Hasan Mahmud through the vacant slips cordon for boundaries. But on 30 Mehidy produced a beautiful ball, pitching in line then turning sharply to take Carey’s outside edge to wicketkeeper Litton Das. He struck again soon after, bowling Webster for five to leave Australia 193-6 and in deep trouble. A famous victory edged ever closer when Australia captain Pat Cummins pushed forward to a Mehidy delivery and got an inside edge to short leg, where Shadman Islam took a sharp chance. Australia were 207-7, still 21 runs behind Bangladesh’s first-innings total. Green and Mitchell Starc batted sensibly to ensure Bangladesh had to bat again. Starc fell for 18 caught behind but Green was playing well and brought up his century shortly after lunch. But despite looking increasingly comfortable, he was undone when a Hasan ball kept low, hit the toe end of his bat and cannoned into the stumps. Mehidy wrapped up the innings when he trapped Nathan Lyon plumb in front leg before. Depsite losing Tanzid in the first over, Mominul and Shadman Islam cruised to victory.

items.title: Messi misses penalty as Nashville hammer Inter Miami 4-1 in MLS
items.description: Lionel Messi missed yet another penalty and was booked as Inter Miami suffered a 4-1 loss at Nashville on Saturday in a top-of-the-table MLS clash. England’s Sam Surridge and Germany’s Hany Mukhtar scored second-half goals for the hosts in a showdown between the Major League Soccer overall leaders. Argentina and Miami captain Messi was denied from the penalty spot in the first half and issued a yellow card in the 59th minute but also assisted Inter’s lone goal. Messi struck both posts in second-half stoppage time. Nashville leads MLS with 43 points and a record of 13-2 with four drawn while Inter Miami are second on 38 points. Nashville had already knocked Miami out of this year’s CONCACAF Champions Cup in the round of 16. Defending MLS champion Miami, which had been a league-best 8-1-1 on the road, saw a seven-match undefeated MLS run snapped as Nashville remained unbeaten at home in the MLS campaign. Honduran defender Andy Najar scored with a header in the 17th minute to give Nashville a 1-0 lead. Miami had a chance to equalize with a Messi penalty kick in the 23rd minute but Nashville goalkeeper Brian Schwake saved his weak effort. Messi’s record from the penalty spot is poor by his sky-high standards, including missing twice at the World Cup. The visitors netted the equalizer three minutes into first-half stoppage time when Venezuelan Telasco Segovia blasted in a right-footed shot off an assist by Messi. Mukhtar, the 2022 MLS Most Valuable Player, put Nashville back in front in the 49th minute. Surridge gave Nashville a 3-1 lead and Mukhtar added his second in the 63rd for extra insurance as the hosts pulled away. items.title: NCAA to automate baggage tracking
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, has concluded plans to mandate the use of Radio Frequency Identification, RFID, baggage tracking technology across Nigerian airports. The move is part of the regulator’s efforts to eliminate the growing incidence of delayed, missing and mishandled baggage at domestic and international terminals. The automated system will replace the traditional barcode-based framework, enabling airlines and passengers to track checked baggage in real time from the point of check-in to final reclaim, without requiring a direct line of sight. Speaking at a stakeholders’ engagement forum held at the NCAA Annex in Lagos, the Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection at the NCAA, Mr Michael Achimugu, said: “For many years now, one of the biggest complaints in the industry has been that of baggage, it is either passengers’ bags have been short-landed, missing, lost, or destroyed. “After delayed flights, baggage issues are the biggest problem. So, what we have decided to do is improve the system by automating it. The technology we are looking to use now is RFID to replace the current technology being used. Standard regulations allow airlines up to seven days to locate and reconcile short-landed baggage with domestic travelers. With RFID tracking, missing or misrouted luggage can be identified and located instantly. Even while you have boarded, you can check to be sure that your bag is on that flight. “And if for any unforeseen circumstance your bag has not landed with you, you can tell even without complaining to the airline where your bag is. So, when you call to complain, you can tell them specifically that you have landed in Lagos, but your bag is in Enugu.” The NCAA also said traditional barcodes require ground handlers to manually align a laser scanner with a printed paper tag on every luggage. If a tag is twisted, torn, dirty, or obscured, the scanner fails to read it. RFID tags, by contrast, embed a tiny microchip and antenna that broadcast location data via radio waves. Scanners can instantly read multiple tags through containers, baggage belts, and cargo holds without needing a direct line-of-sight. While the technical implementation is being driven in collaboration with the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, as the infrastructure owner, the NCAA is currently reviewing civil aviation regulations to make automated RFID tracking mandatory for all airlines operating within Nigerian airspace. items.title: Olu of Warri warns: We shouldn’t call our neighbours slaves again
items.description: •As monarch, Ovie of Agbarha ‘commit to peace, growth’ in oil-rich city By Jimitota Onoyume Olu of Warri Ogiame Atuwatse III and his counterpart, His Royal Majesty Kingsley Emakpo Orereh, Igbi II, the Ovie of Agbarha, have both committed to unity, peace and unhindered development in Warri, Delta State. The monarchs, in their separate speeches yesterday at the Warri Unity Football Game held at the Federal Government College Warri, as part of the activities for the 5th coronation anniversary of the Olu of Warri, recalled the glorious era of peace, unity and love among the tribes in the oil rich city, promising to sustain the rich values. The Olu of Warri also proclaimed that henceforth no Itsekiri son or daughter should address or describe anyone in the oil-rich city as slave. “In our palace, we have officially prohibited our people from referring to our neighbours as slaves. That word is no longer tolerated in the palace of the Olu of Warri — and we say it today for the whole world to hear”, the monarch said. “The coronation anniversary of Ogiame Atuwatse III — however long God grants this reign — shall be devoted to unity, to peace, to progress, and to prosperity. A declaration before the world “As leader of the Itsekiri nation, we are playing our own part, and we want it placed on public record. “And all of us, every tribe, every tongue, every family that calls this place home — shall enjoy the fruit of it, in peace and in good health. “Warri will never carry last again. “Today, we humbly stretch out our hand and say — let us begin anew. “With respect, and with mutual benefit, we cannot build a new vision through old lenses, carrying old grudges and old suspicions. We are not speaking through any intermediary”. On his part, the Ovie of Agbarha Igbi II, who addressed the mammoth gathering in Urhobo, Itsekiri and English languages, said he grew up in Okere, stressing that then there was no division between the Itsekiri and Urhobo. He harped on the urgent need for unity in Warri, commending the Olu for initiating the Warri unity Game. The monarch also appealed for an end to hate speeches targeted at ethnic groups on social media. His words: “I grew up in Okere. I did not know I was Urhobo. It was later in life I started hearing that this one is Urhobo while this is Itsekiri. “In my growing days you hardly heard of this divide. We were all united. Let the unity continue. “I thank Ogiame for the unity game today. It will consolidate unity among us. I also enjoin those in social media hurling insults to stop it. Let us not sell ourselves to strangers”. It was an epochal moment at the venue of the Unity Game when the two monarchs held their hands. The post Olu of Warri warns: We shouldn’t call our neighbours slaves again appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: N24BN DELTA LG MONEY: My blackmailers claimed to have EFCC, ICPC in their pockets – Burutu council chair
items.description: · Wants anti-graft agencies to intervene By Chancel Bomadi Sunday Chief Julius Takeme is the Chairman of Burutu Local Government Area of Delta State. Previously, he held the position of Transition Chairman for the council area and is a native of Obotebe community in the riverine council area. In this interview, Takeme reveals that his administration has made significant strides in enhancing infrastructural development and preserving the essential peace and stability in the oil-rich council area, among other matters. Excerpts: You have led Burutu for over two years; could you share the initiatives you have implemented for the benefit of the council area? We have made remarkable strides in infrastructural development, alongside promoting peace and security across various communities in the local government area. By God’s grace, the council has embarked on numerous infrastructural projects at the council headquarters and in various communities. Currently, there are ongoing projects such as the new Council Secretariat Complex, which includes the chairman’s office duplex, administrative blocks, chairman’s lodge, a 4,000-capacity conference hall, chapel, vice chairman’s office and other facilities. We are also constructing a new Legislative Chamber, a VIP Lodge, and other ongoing projects in Burutu. Furthermore, over two thousand women are employed to maintain cleanliness in Burutu, the council headquarters. In terms of healthcare, we have renovated the Primary Healthcare Centres in various communities within the council area, ensuring they are equipped to provide quality healthcare services to the people living in the creek. In discussing the maintenance of peace and security within the council area, particularly in multinational host communities, we have performed commendably. The council has intervened and resolved disputes concerning community leadership struggles among aspirants in various creek communities. We have addressed and settled intra-communal leadership conflicts in Tuomo, Ojobo, Enekorogha, Okpokunou, Ayakoromo, and other communities. I assure you that we are committed to excelling in human capital empowerment by actively engaging the young people in meaningful activities. Furthermore, we have launched free medical outreach programmes for our people, offering treatment for a variety of illnesses and diseases. We will continue to work for the people of Burutu local government area. You might be interested to learn that I provided the needed funding for Ms Timipame-ere Akiayefa, an indigene of Torugbene community, who represented Nigeria to the Commonwealth Games in Singapore, and who won a gold medal in the swimming competitions. I believe we can do much more for people in delivering the democracy dividends as part of the vision of our hardworking governor’s Renewed Hope for MORE Agenda. There are allegations from some individuals on social media, claiming to be former chairmanship aspirants in the state. They assert that you owe them and have not undertaken any significant projects to justify the 23.7 billion naira federal allocation to the council since you assumed office. How do you respond to these allegations? As a journalist, I’m sure you have visited Burutu and observed our efforts and achievements, as I previously mentioned, including the jobs we have completed and commissioned, as well as the ongoing projects. The essence of leadership lies in the judicious application of resources to improve the lives of the people, which is the hallmark of good governance. When we assumed office, I promised the people of Burutu that I would provide people-oriented services, and that is precisely what we are doing in Burutu local government area. We are transforming Burutu through human capital development and the delivery of infrastructural advancements. Currently, all our ongoing projects are significant landmarks, as I mentioned earlier. You will also agree with me on the challenges posed by the terrain, where it requires approximately four times the effort needed to construct any structure in the cities—considering transportation, logistics, loading and unloading of building materials and equipment, and so forth. Regarding the allegation of misappropriation in which it is claimed that someone has mismanaged approximately 24 billion naira over twenty-four months, as we approach our 24-month tenure, it implies that one billion naira is allocated to Burutu local government area monthly, which is both fallacious and absurd. I am uncertain of the sources from which the person making this claim derived this information. In terms of accountability, I regularly present myself before the Burutu Legislative Assembly to report my activities to the councillors. Those making these allegations identify themselves as former aspirants and are all aware of the processes that led to the selection of candidates for the former ruling party in the state at that time. It was the party’s internal democratic procedure, involving a form of mock primaries, which is well-known to all of us. It is important to note that none of them purchased nomination forms prior to my selection as a candidate, as the party had decided not to sell forms. Following the local government elections, where the party triumphed across the state, it became imperative for me to include everyone in the decision-making process to foster unity within the party in the council area. A wise politician must always embrace this principle to ensure cohesion. Consequently, under my leadership, Burutu remains united, with no factions within the ruling APC in Burutu local government area. In their initial social media post, the so-called former aspirants under an association alleged that I am indebted to them, alluding to my generous decision to include them in the provision of financial support and assistance to them. Imagine, one guy called me on phone and threatened that I had not known him yet, that he had the EFCC and ICPC connections. He said if I refused to yield to their financial demands, he would ask the anti-graft agencies to come after me. He also promised to blackmail me before the governor. Really? I asked. Shortly after the threat, the posts emerged on social media. Now, I have decided that enough is enough. How can someone claim to have Federal Government agencies in his pockets and be using them to do his biddings? How! It is clear that this is their modus operandi, as they have not rendered any service or job to me or to Burutu local government council. They have also made it clear that they are fraternizing with the opposition PDP. I wish to use this medium to urge the EFCC and ICPC to investigate these so-called former aspirants who are blackmailing me and misinforming the public about the administration of Burutu local government council. I believe this is one method used to extort money from a coerced public office holder. How do you evaluate Gov Oborevwori’s performance in terms service delivery to Deltans? Marvelous! Gov Sheriff Oborevwori has justified the confidence Deltans have placed in him. Observing the ongoing developmental strides in the state, one can attest to the fact that the governor has exceeded the people’s expectations in just his first term in office. If he were focusing on a single sector in his developmental efforts, critics might have claimed that he was only concentrating on infrastructure, such as the construction of bridges and road networks. However, this is not the case. He has performed exceptionally well across various sectors, particularly in healthcare facilities, human empowerment schemes, civil servants’ welfare, economic development and more. Recently, the governor’s wife, Deaconess Mrs. Tobore Oborevwori, initiated a free healthcare outreach in Burutu local government area through her charity organization, You Matter Foundation. Humanitarian services were offered to the vulnerable and individuals with special needs in Kiagbodo. This initiative is a welcome development for Deltans, as the foundation is expanding its outreach programmes to the various federal constituencies across the state. It is all part of the effort of our able governor to deliver the dividends of democracy to the people. The Ayakoromo Bridge project is now receiving the necessary attention from the government, and I believe that between now and early next year, the project will be commissioned. Once commissioned, this project will open up the oil-rich riverine area of the state to investors. Indeed, all the initiatives the governor has undertaken in the riverine part of the state, particularly in Burutu local government area, are remarkable and transformative. Some of these projects include the already commissioned Ogulagha—Odimodi road, Egodor—Ogboingbene road (Phase 2), Technical College at Kiagbodo, Torugbene-Ojobo road, and various internal roads within communities in the creeks. Gov Oborevwori stands out for his distinctive approach to project initiation and execution across the state. However, like Oliver Twist, we wish to make a special appeal to our industrious governor to initiate the construction of a road connecting Old Burutu town, the headquarters of the oil-rich local government area of Delta State. I am confident that the name associated with the commencement of this road will be remembered for a millennium. I humbly urge our dynamic governor and leader to prioritize this project upon reelection for a second term. A survey plan already exists, indicating that Burutu can be more easily accessed by road, and I propose that the road be constructed in phases for convenience. If you were to evaluate the governor’s performance in terms of percentage, what score would you assign him? Based on my observations throughout the state, if I were to evaluate Governor Oborevwori’s performance in terms of percentage, as a reasonable and progressive Deltan rather than a politician, I would assign him a score of 101%. With the 2027 general elections fast approaching, how prepared is your party at the local government level? No shaking! We are steadfast and well-prepared, the people of Burutu Local Government Area are ready to vote overwhelmingly for the ruling APC, as there is no opposition here. As I mentioned earlier, Burutu is now a united entity, and we are aligned in the decision-making process. We, the people of Burutu Local Government Area, believe that the 2027 general elections are the opportune moment to reciprocate the goodwill of our esteemed governor by voting en masse for the party to ensure his return for continuity. There is no contest here; we are APC, and all the leaders of Burutu have agreed to deliver Bulk Vote for the party to secure the return of our governor, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and all candidates under the party. We understand that casting our votes for the APC is the only way to express our gratitude to Governor Oborevwori for including Burutu Local Government in his Renewed Hope for MORE Agenda. Your final words Under my leadership as council chairman, Burutu will continue to be a peaceful place where development can flourish in all communities. I am committed to working tirelessly for the unity, peace and progress of our people and the council area. The post N24BN DELTA LG MONEY: My blackmailers claimed to have EFCC, ICPC in their pockets – Burutu council chair appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 18 Years After: RMAFC moves to review president, governors, lawmakers’ pay
items.description: By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor The Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission, RMAFC, has completed the review of the remuneration of political office holders, 18 years after their salaries were last reviewed by law, saying the proposed new remuneration and revenue allocation Bills will reach the National Assembly before the end of the year. Chairman of RMAFC, Dr Mohammed Bello Shehu, disclosed this yesterday at a breakfast session with members of the Guild of Editors in Lagos. Shehu said the remuneration review covered the president, governors, deputy governors, legislators and other political office holders, stressing that the existing salary structure was based on legislation dating back to 2007/2008. “From 2008 to date, the salaries of not only legislators but also ministers, governors and the President have not been reviewed by law”, he said. “The Commission attempted to review them twice — once in 2013 and again in 2022. But both President Goodluck Jonathan and President Muhammadu Buhari, for whatever reasons, were unable to transmit the review to the National Assembly. “Where we are now, as far as we know and as far as every organisation is aware, the salaries of legislators — senators and members of the House of Representatives — still remain those contained in the Act of 2007/2008. They have not changed”. According to him, the latest review has been completed and is being processed in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Justice. “We have completed the process. Very soon, the President will receive the package and it will be transmitted to the National Assembly. “We have sent a copy to Mr. President. We have also gone to the Ministry of Justice. They have drafted a new Act. They have drafted a new one and sent it back to us. We are looking at it to ensure conformity with what we have done. “After that, we will take it to Mr. President and say: ‘Sir, we think it is time for you to send this to the National Assembly for them to make it an Act.’” Shehu argued that the prolonged stagnation of political office holders’ salaries was no longer sustainable, noting that the cost of living had changed considerably since 2008. “The Commission is an advocate of fair wages for fair work. If you give a minister less than N1 million a month, come on, that is not reasonable. “The salary of a minister is less than N1 million a month. My commissioners here are Federal Commissioners, and their salaries are also less than N1 million a month. These salaries have not been reviewed from 2008 to date”. He added that better remuneration could help reduce incentives for corruption. “I believe that political office holders should be paid something reasonable so that they can operate effectively and reduce the temptation for corruption. “You cannot have the salary of this class of people stagnant from 2008 until now. And anytime you say you want to raise it, everybody will react negatively. What you are effectively doing is allowing them to go and become corrupt for whatever they want to do. That is not good for the system.” On revenue allocation, Shehu said RMAFC had also completed a new formula designed to reflect additional responsibilities being assumed by state governments. His words: “We have made adjustments, and now we have completed the process. Mr. President is aware. We are working in collaboration with the Ministry of Justice to draft the enabling Act. Once it is ready, Mr. President will transmit it to the National Assembly. “My members here, the Plenary of the Commission, have approved the new formula”. He said the Commission expected the remuneration and revenue allocation Bills to be ready before the end of the year. LG autonomy On local government autonomy, Shehu said RMAFC had established monitoring committees for both state and local governments to ensure proper utilisation of allocations. “The Commission used to monitor local governments previously, and we have now set up a Local Government Monitoring Committee and a State Monitoring Committee.” The post 18 Years After: RMAFC moves to review president, governors, lawmakers’ pay appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: POLITICS OF THE BIG TENT
items.description: In Europe and the United States, the post-1945 era marked a shift from ‘mass parties’ to broad ‘big-tent’ parties. Mass parties had operated on strict class lines. Democratic socialist outfits appealed to industrial workers, while conservative parties represented business elites and religious traditionalists. Big-tent politics had already taken root in North America due to its vast geography, rapid industrialisation, and diverse immigrant and Black populations. To build winning national majorities, the Democratic and Republican parties developed broad platforms, accommodating competing internal factions under a shared umbrella and a loose ideological core. This was the beginning of big-tent parties. The Democratic Party in the US, especially from the early 1930s onwards, has housed democratic socialists, progressives, social liberals and pro-business centrists, alongside its conservative Southern wing, which existed within the party till the early 1960s. The latter was mainly to bag votes from the ‘Bible belt’ states. The modern Republican Party functions as a broad umbrella encompassing social conservatives, Christian nationalists, fiscal centrists and right-wing populists. A similar evolution occurred in western Europe after World War II. According to the German jurist Otto Kirchheimer, as the post-war economic growth expanded the middle-class, most voters began to favour pragmatic moderation over class antagonism. Left-wing parties, such as the UK Labour Party and Germany’s Social Democratic Party, shifted toward a progressive centre-left stance, while centre-right parties, such as the British Conservatives and Germany’s Christian Democrats, softened their hard social moralism and elitism to capture votes from across the classes. Political scientists mostly view big-tent parties as important democratic stabilisers. By absorbing diverse economic, regional and social groups, a big-tent outfit facilitates them to negotiate and form a consensus under a single umbrella. This prevents extreme polarisation and avoids the chaotic parliamentary fragmentation typical of unstable multiparty systems that lack big-tent parties. From the Democrats and Republicans in the United States to the PPP, PML-N and PTI in Pakistan, the very diversity that makes big-tent parties electorally powerful can also become their greatest vulnerability Big-tent outfits combine diverse demands and elements, transforming societal rivalries into organised, workable governing units. The success of a big-tent party depends on how they design mechanisms to manage internal dissent. Rather than enforcing monolithic obedience, party structures use primary elections, regional quotas and factional appointments to give diverse interest groups a seat at tables that matter. This internal diplomacy allows the overarching party to remain flexible. A well-managed big-tent party can position its platform across different political cycles, moving slightly leftward or rightward to keep pace with changing electorate moods, without suffering an electoral decline. Following the 1947 Partition , India saw a classic big-tent system emerge under the Indian National Congress (INC). Operating on a secular, centre-left platform, Congress absorbed diverse socialist, moderate and regional groups to maintain a 30-year political monopoly. As the nation’s founding party, it offered a shared national brand that co-opted multiple local political elites and bridged vast linguistic and religious divides. INC’s dominance was broken in 1977 by the Janata Party (JP). JP was a broad anti-INC coalition of secular, regional, Hindutva and left-wing groups who couldn’t find a place under INC’s tent. However, JP illustrated a common pitfall related to big-tent politics: unmanaged factional infighting. Driven by intense ideological friction and personal rivalries among its leadership, JP collapsed from within after just three years in power. When internal fractures widen in big-tent parties, the parties tend to lose their electoral appeal or fall prey to radical internal takeovers. This occurred within the US Republican Party, where the right-wing populist Maga (Make America Great Again) movement led by Donald Trump weaponised primary elections to displace the Republican Party’s dominant free market and moderate factions. The populist wing of the party then reoriented the outfit into becoming a nationalist-populist vehicle. But this transformation has introduced severe vulnerabilities, driven by infighting within the party’s populist wing, foreign policy controversies and an increasing backlash in the US against Israeli lobby groups such as the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac). Trump’s approval ratings have plummeted . The Democrats are facing their own internal tensions. Key primary victories by progressive candidates of the party have alarmed its centrist factions, who fear left-leaning Democrats could alienate moderate voters in upcoming national contests. In South Asia, apart from INC and then JP, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) began to function as a big-tent party. Historically a Hindu nationalist party with an upper-caste base, the BJP began to widen its umbrella. It started to accommodate distinct groups: Hindutva hardliners, big business groups, populists and pragmatists absorbed from opposition parties. Hindutva remains the BJP’s ideological anchor, though, even as it increasingly applies big-tent electoral strategies. Pakistan developed a big-tent model led by the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N). Before these, Pakistan’s founding party, the Muslim League, had successfully managed to combine a wide range of left to right groups to win enough seats in the 1946 elections in British India, which allowed it to push for a separate Muslim-majority country. But after the creation of Pakistan, friction between different groups in the League became so intense that the party fractured. The PPP, formed in 1967, shaped a centre-left core with diverse leftist, progressive, liberal and centrist groups, while the PML-N, formed in 1992, united urban pro-business cohorts, landed elites, centrists and social conservatives. In 2011, facilitated by the then military establishment, the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) expanded into a third big-tent party by absorbing traditional ‘electables’ from the two existing big-tent outfits. PTI operated as an archetypal contemporary populist party, weaving a flexible and performative core of right- and left-wing tropes around a central anti-corruption narrative and personal loyalty to its leader. This vague ideological architecture allowed urban middle-class youth, conservatives, landed elites and mainstream Islamists to coexist under one banner. However, like India’s Janata Party, PTI struggled to manage its internal frictions and rapidly unravelled once its top leader was removed from power and imprisoned. Big-tent parties remain double-edged constructs. While their capacity to combine diverse interests and build broad platforms shields democracies against fragmentation, their reliance on a conflicted ideological core and mismanaged internal conflicts leaves them vulnerable. This requires continuous maintenance. Without disciplined leadership, big-tent parties risk devolving into factional warfare, opening the door to radical takeovers or collapse when internal consensus breaks down. Maintaining a workable equilibrium remains a constant challenge. In Pakistan, big-tent parties such as the PML-N and the PPP have done remarkably well to avoid disintegration despite attempts by previous military establishments to dismantle them by exploiting their internal frictions. This ability to regroup and survive is something that PTI has, so far, failed to demonstrate. Published in Dawn, EOS, August 16th, 2026
